1: # AGENTS.md — read this first

3: ## What we're building
4: 
5: **ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
6: **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
7: **Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
8: HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
9: prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
10: **Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
11: Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).
12: 
13: ## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)
14: 
15: - **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
16:   for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
17:   every decision.
18: - **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
19:   market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
20: - **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
21:   We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
22: - **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
23:   competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
24:   requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
25:   them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
26: - **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
27:   priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
28:   a decision status.
29: - **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
30:   design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
31:   and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
32:   pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
33: - **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
34:   handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
35:   beats shallow coverage of everything.
36: - **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
37:   requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
38:   business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_
39: 
40: ## Rules for every agent
41: 
42: 1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
43:    something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
44: 2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
45:    contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
46: 3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
47:    publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
48:    and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
49:    Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or

51: 4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
52:    sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
53: 5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
54:    requirement writes an AuditEvent.
55: 6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
56:    `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
57:    the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.

40: /** JSON semantics, recursive lexical key ordering, and explicit rejection of non-JSON content. */
41: export function filterHash(value: unknown): string {
42:   const ancestors = new Set<object>();
43:   function sorted(v: unknown): unknown {
44:     if (v === undefined) return undefined;
45:     if (v === null || typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "boolean") return v;
46:     if (typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v)) return v;
47:     if (typeof v !== "object" || ancestors.has(v))
48:       throw new Error("AI Filter requires acyclic JSON input.");
49:     if (
50:       !Array.isArray(v) &&
51:       Object.getPrototypeOf(v) !== Object.prototype &&
52:       Object.getPrototypeOf(v) !== null
53:     )
54:       throw new Error("AI Filter requires plain JSON input.");
55:     ancestors.add(v);
56:     const result = Array.isArray(v)
57:       ? v.map(sorted)
58:       : Object.fromEntries(
59:           Object.keys(v)
60:             .sort()
61:             .map((key) => [key, sorted((v as Record<string, unknown>)[key])]),
62:         );
63:     ancestors.delete(v);
64:     return result;
65:   }
66:   try {
67:     const json = JSON.stringify(sorted(value));
68:     if (json === undefined) throw new Error();
69:     return createHash("sha256").update(json).digest("hex");
70:   } catch {
71:     throw new Error("AI Filter requires finite, acyclic JSON input.");
72:   }
73: }

75: function fieldValue(item: unknown, field: string): unknown {
76:   const object = item as Record<string, unknown>;
77:   if (Object.hasOwn(object, field)) return object[field];
78:   const fields = object.fields;
79:   if (fields && typeof fields === "object" && Object.hasOwn(fields, field))
80:     return (fields as Record<string, unknown>)[field];
81:   let value: unknown = item;
82:   for (const segment of field.split(".")) {
83:     if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || !Object.hasOwn(value, segment)) return undefined;
84:     value = (value as Record<string, unknown>)[segment];
85:   }
86:   return value;
87: }

4:   if (!PipelineData.safeParse(input).success) throw new Error("AI Filter input is invalid.");
5:   const maps = Object.fromEntries(
6:     DATA_KEYS.map((key) => [
7:       key,
8:       new Map<string, { id: string }>(input[key].map((item) => [item.id, item])),
9:     ]),
10:   ) as Record<DataKey, Map<string, { id: string }>>;
11:   for (const key of DATA_KEYS) {
12:     if (maps[key].size !== input[key].length)
13:       throw new Error(`AI Filter input has duplicate ${key} IDs.`);
14:   }
15:   const records = new Map(input.records.map((item) => [item.id, item]));
16:   for (const finding of input.findings) {
17:     for (const ref of finding.evidence) {
18:       const record = ref.recordId ? records.get(ref.recordId) : undefined;
19:       if (record && (record.sourceId !== ref.sourceId || !record.text.includes(ref.excerpt)))
20:         throw new Error("AI Filter available evidence has inconsistent source or excerpt.");
21:     }
22:   }
23:   const primary: DataKey =
24:     (["requirements", "themes", "findings", "records"] as const).find((key) => input[key].length) ??
25:     "sources";
26:   const themes = new Map(input.themes.map((item) => [item.id, item]));
27:   const findings = new Map(input.findings.map((item) => [item.id, item]));
28:   const requirements = new Map(input.requirements.map((item) => [item.id, item]));
29:   const themesByFinding = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
30:   for (const theme of input.themes) {
31:     for (const id of theme.findingIds) {
32:       const refs = themesByFinding.get(id) ?? new Set<string>();
33:       refs.add(theme.id);
34:       themesByFinding.set(id, refs);
35:     }
36:   }
37:   for (const finding of input.findings) {
38:     if (!finding.themeId) continue;
39:     const theme = themes.get(finding.themeId);
40:     if (theme && !theme.findingIds.includes(finding.id))
41:       throw new Error("AI Filter available theme and finding references are inconsistent.");
42:   }
43:   function membership() {
44:     return Object.fromEntries(DATA_KEYS.map((key) => [key, new Set<string>()])) as Record<
45:       DataKey,
46:       Set<string>
47:     >;
48:   }
49:   function select(ids: ReturnType<typeof membership>): PipelineData {
50:     return {
51:       ...input,
52:       ...Object.fromEntries(
53:         DATA_KEYS.map((key) => [key, input[key].filter((item) => ids[key].has(item.id))]),
54:       ),
55:     } as PipelineData;
56:   }
57:   function closure(layer: DataKey, id: string) {
58:     const ids = membership();
59:     const pending: [DataKey, string][] = [];
60:     function add(key: DataKey, ref: string) {
61:       if (ids[key].has(ref)) return;
62:       if (!maps[key].has(ref)) {
63:         warnings.add(
64:           `Unavailable referenced ${key}; original links preserved, no evidence invented.`,
65:         );
66:         return;
67:       }
68:       ids[key].add(ref);
69:       pending.push([key, ref]);
70:     }
71:     add(layer, id);
72:     for (let cursor = 0; cursor < pending.length; cursor++) {
73:       const [key, ref] = pending[cursor]!;
74:       switch (key) {
75:         case "requirements": {
76:           const item = requirements.get(ref)!;
77:           for (const findingId of [...item.findingIds, ...item.conflictingFindingIds])
78:             add("findings", findingId);
79:           for (const sourceId of item.sourceIds) add("sources", sourceId);
80:           break;
81:         }
82:         case "themes":
83:           for (const findingId of themes.get(ref)!.findingIds) add("findings", findingId);
84:           for (const finding of input.findings)
85:             if (finding.themeId === ref) add("findings", finding.id);
86:           break;
87:         case "findings": {
88:           const item = findings.get(ref)!;
89:           if (item.themeId) add("themes", item.themeId);
90:           for (const themeId of themesByFinding.get(ref) ?? []) add("themes", themeId);
91:           for (const evidence of item.evidence) {
92:             add("sources", evidence.sourceId);
93:             if (evidence.recordId) add("records", evidence.recordId);
94:           }
95:           break;
96:         }
97:         case "records":
98:           add("sources", records.get(ref)!.sourceId);
99:           break;
100:         case "sources":
101:           break;
102:       }
103:     }
104:     return ids;
105:   }
106:   // Validate/report missing links even for items later excluded, without resurrecting them.
107:   for (const key of DATA_KEYS) for (const item of input[key]) closure(key, item.id);
108:   return { primary, membership, select, closure };
109: }

   **File:** `/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL-ai-filter/packages/llm/src/mock.ts:523–549`
